policy.scope: Project creation and conditional follow-up generation for the curated profiles; documentation guidance, not an execution service or integration certification.
instructions: Before writing a new project's application files, read its profile's starting points and use the official framework or language initializer appropriate to the component. Do not hand-recreate a generated skeleton. Where no full application generator exists, use the documented module/package initializer and assemble only the missing application pieces.

Choose one starting point per component. Check the installed generator's version and help, prerequisites, template, database, UI, test and runtime options. Commands are examples: replace names and paths, resolve compatible versions, and record the exact invocation and selected options. Do not blindly run every listed generator.

Generate in a new empty destination. For an existing repository, preserve its conventions and use relevant incremental generators. If a baseline comparison is needed, generate a separate disposable reference with matching versions/options and reconcile deliberately; never regenerate over existing work.

Keep applicable generated configuration, hidden files, formatter/linter settings, ignore rules, manifests, lockfiles, tests, wrappers and entry points. Extend them for the project instead of replacing them with abbreviated handwritten copies. A generator may initialize version control or offer a commit; respect the user's Git instructions.

Run the generated baseline's documented checks before feature changes, then relevant checks after configuration and implementation. Inspect what version control would include, including hidden files, build output, local secrets and operating-system metadata. Add needed ignore rules explicitly: no generator guarantees that .DS_Store or every local artifact is ignored.

Use follow-up generators only when their feature or tool is selected. Review generated changes and dependencies, apply required migrations in the intended environment, and exercise the generated behavior. Scaffolding does not establish authorization, safe retries, production readiness or every best practice.

If the required generator, template or IDE is unavailable, report the missing prerequisite and the documented route. Do not silently substitute a handwritten scaffold. Keep documentation review, generator execution, baseline checks and application qualification as separate evidence.
receipt: Component and selected starting point, or the documented absence of a full application generator
Generator/toolchain versions, exact commands or IDE template/settings, working directory and generated destination
Generated files retained, deliberate deviations with reasons, and required supplemental ignore rules
Baseline checks and later checks actually run, results and remaining prerequisites or untested behavior

Set the real site URL and verify canonical metadata and sitemap against production host configuration. Check redirect status and trailing-slash behavior at that host; static output may express redirects as HTML rather than an HTTP status.
Verify image transformations and direct public asset URLs. If video is used, test its chosen streaming service and do not attribute video handling to Astro.

If adding an adapter or CMS, test its actual preview, draft privacy, authorization, cookies, redirects, runtime APIs, cache behavior and production deployment separately. No application integration test or static regression suite was run for this record.
integration_steps: From the generated project root, write README purpose, start commands, content source and editorial owner, public URL policy and navigation to installed Astro documentation. Preserve the user's existing repository instructions.

Create Content Collections only when structured Markdown/data needs schema validation; define the schema and explicit static page routes together. Keep static public content distinct from draft or account-specific content.

Document the content-route and URL map, canonical domain, trailing-slash rule, 404 behavior, redirects and the host setting that implements each. Confirm whether static redirect output provides the required response status; if not, configure a host redirect rule or select an adapter route and verify it.

Set the production site URL and generate a sitemap only when required. Review canonical URLs, duplicate routes, metadata, indexability and actual generated HTML; SEO metadata does not establish search indexing.

Assign media ownership explicitly. Use src image imports for supported processing, public files for unprocessed stable paths, and a selected external service for video streaming. Check license, alt text, dimensions, cache and delivery on the deployed host.

For a selected CMS, keep the CMS authoritative for editorial content, drafts and assets. Specify build/webhook ownership, preview and draft authorization before connecting it; do not leak preview tokens into client islands or static output.

Keep existing APIs, identity, database, migrations, jobs and external effects with their current owners. A static Astro client can consume public or authenticated API endpoints as designed, but static files cannot contain secrets or provide request-time permission checks. If a server-side page or new API is required, define a separate backend/adapter migration and its data ownership before implementation.

Run the project build and dev server; inspect generated route HTML, direct URLs, assets and not-found behavior. Against the intended host, verify redirect status, headers, cache, canonical URL and sitemap. This research did not run application tests, a CMS integration or an adapter deployment.

integration_steps: After completing the selected starting point, read its generated README, mix.exs, mix.lock and runtime pins. Preserve the chosen plain Mix or Phoenix architecture; the following Phoenix integrations apply only when Phoenix is present.

For a Phoenix application, inspect and complete the generated setup alias after configuring development/test database access. Keep credentials outside committed secrets; follow the generator output when a selected omission means an alias or integration is unavailable.

If dependency guidance synchronization is useful, add usage_rules as a development dependency, choose the relevant dependency rules in mix.exs and review mix usage_rules.sync output. Preserve maintained generated guidance; an explicit README-only policy may configure a README-linked alternate file such as docs/dependency-rules.md.

If Phoenix browser accounts are required, complete the authentication follow-up recipe, review its generated instructions and configure transactional email delivery. Keep local/test delivery adapters in their intended environments; verify scopes and permission checks for application operations.

If durable background jobs are required, follow the installed Oban version’s installation and migration instructions, supervise Oban and configure bounded queues. Use supported persistence and idempotent workers; test retry and duplicate-effect handling. A Task is suitable only for explicitly disposable work.

Add development and test checks selected for this project. Formatter, compiler warnings and ExUnit apply to plain Mix applications; Ecto SQL Sandbox, LiveViewTest, Sobelow and other Phoenix-specific checks require their corresponding dependencies and application architecture.

For Phoenix applications that need real-browser verification, install/configure PhoenixTest.Playwright or the selected browser suite with its matching JavaScript dependency and browser binaries. Configure the test endpoint and SQL sandbox as documented; server-side LiveView tests do not establish browser JavaScript or visual correctness.

Run the applicable verification commands and actual application flows, fixing failures in place and retaining evidence. Skip tools whose dependency was not selected rather than claiming their checks passed; do not regenerate over existing work to hide failures.

For deployment qualification, select the intended host and runtime configuration. In Phoenix applications follow the release-helper recipe; build production assets only when the selected application has assets. Build a release compatible with the target OS, architecture and native dependencies.

Before claiming production readiness, rehearse startup, migrations and any applicable reconnect/job-retry behavior on the selected host. Establish secrets, TLS, backups, restore and rollback ownership; a generated release or passing local tests do not establish those outcomes.

Completion: record exact runtime/dependency versions, the application lockfile, selected generation/integration steps, check results and observed flows in README-linked evidence. State any untested deployment or native-mobile paths explicitly.
preserve: Keep generated mix.exs aliases, .formatter.exs, tests/helpers, configuration, runtime supervision and project documentation as the starting base; make deliberate, reviewable changes rather than recreating the scaffold by hand.
Preserve the complete generated .gitignore and add project/platform entries such as .DS_Store as supplements. Do not claim every generator version already ignores macOS metadata.
Retain dependency lockfiles for application reproducibility according to repository policy. Keep credentials, build outputs and dependency caches out of commits.
Existing project conventions and maintained README-linked guidance remain authoritative; generator commands are for new projects or deliberate scoped additions, not destructive replacement.
Record the generator command, versions, selected switches and reasons for deviations with the project setup evidence.
verification: Before generation, inspect installed mix help for each selected task and check the chosen runtime/generator requirements against installed versions; unversioned documentation can describe a newer release.

Inspect the generated files and pending repository diff, including hidden files. Check that formatter configuration, tests/helpers, ignore rules and required application supervision are present for the selected variant.
Run mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test from the generated project root after dependency/database setup. Repair failures in place and record actual results.

For Phoenix browser applications, run mix phx.server and inspect the actual local page and generated flows; for APIs, exercise the intended requests. A server process starting is not a completed interaction check.

Use git status --short --untracked-files=all and git check-ignore -v .DS_Store _build deps to review the selected ignore rules. In a disposable copy or separate index, inspect what staging all files would include; never alter the user index merely to test hygiene.
Confirm generated authentication/scopes and application operations reject unauthorized access; generated CRUD does not settle domain permissions.

commands.purpose: Generate the SDK 58 default Expo project while suppressing generated AGENTS.md and Claude settings. During the documented SDK 58 transition, explicitly pin `default@sdk-58`; inspect generated files and repository state. Defer dependency installation so the next step installs packages once from the generated project root.
Install the generated package manifest and create the project's lockfile. Keep the resolved versions in that lockfile.
Check that installed Expo/React Native packages match the selected SDK; inspect installed-version help if the command differs.

notes: Observed 23 October 2026 with the explicit `default@sdk-58` template: create-expo-app 5.1.5 generated Expo SDK 58.0.17, React Native 0.88.0, React 19.3.0 and Expo Router 58.0.25 in package.json. npm install completed; Expo Doctor passed 20/20; `npx expo export --platform ios` emitted a JS bundle. Generated `npm run lint` failed with a version-check error despite ESLint 9.39.5 being installed; direct ESLint found a generated React Hooks rule violation, and `tsc --noEmit` found generated CSS/type compatibility errors. These checks do not establish native build/device compatibility.

The reviewed `default@sdk-58` command with --no-install and --no-agents-md created .git/ with an initial commit. Current help exposed no --no-git option. For a monorepo, decide the intended Git root before generation and resolve nested Git ownership explicitly; never run the initializer over an existing application.

Expo docs state that during the SDK 58 transition `create-expo-app@latest` without `--template` creates SDK 57; pin `--template default@sdk-58` when SDK 58 is the intended baseline. The pinned template was successfully generated in a disposable directory on 23 October 2026.
The default template includes Expo Router, TypeScript and a web target. The existence of generated web files does not qualify a browser product or make this profile a web-stack recommendation.

Expo Go is a limited playground with a fixed set of native libraries. Production development should use a development build; custom native code and native dependencies absent from Expo Go require one.

Default CNG projects generate native iOS/Android directories from app config and plugins. Prefer config plugins for repeatable project configuration; direct edits to generated native directories can be overwritten by prebuild.
`--no-install` can defer npm and native package installation when inspecting a disposable scaffold; install and verify the actual project's dependencies before developing.

follow_up_generators.when: The app needs a native module not bundled in Expo Go, custom native code, native configuration, app identity changes to verify, or representative production-like testing.
steps: Check the selected library's iOS and Android support, config plugin, Expo SDK compatibility, minimum OS/SDK and required permissions.

Choose a local native toolchain or an explicitly selected EAS cloud build. Local iOS building requires macOS/Xcode; local Android building requires Android Studio, Android SDK and a compatible Java toolchain. Cloud builds move compilation to EAS but do not eliminate device tests, app-account ownership or store credentials.
Generate native directories/build a development client using the project's current Expo CLI and documented workflow. Review generated diffs; use config plugins for repeatable native configuration.
Install and exercise the development build on both platforms. Rebuild after changes to native dependencies, plugins or app configuration.

commands.purpose: Build and launch the iOS app locally for a simulator or configured device. This is not an App Store-signed release.

commands.purpose: Build and launch the Android app locally. Discover the actual variant/toolchain and inspect the generated Gradle project.
Diagnose app config, dependency compatibility and common project health issues; it does not replace native builds or device checks.

notes: Expo Go cannot load arbitrary native code. Rebuild the development client when the native dependency set or native configuration changes.

When using Continuous Native Generation, generated android/ios directories are normally regenerated from app config and plugins. Keep intentional platform customization reproducible and review source-control ownership before committing generated native projects.

EAS Build is optional. Account linking, build credentials, signing, push credentials and store submission are separate project decisions; this guidance does not create accounts or establish release readiness.

follow_up_generators.name: App-local Expo native module
follow_up_generators.when: A requirement genuinely needs custom Swift or Kotlin native functionality and no maintained compatible module meets it; use a local module when only this application needs it.

commands.purpose: Use Expo's documented local-module generator to create an app-local native module; inspect current CLI help and generated iOS/Android code before adopting it.

notes: A local module introduces native code and needs development builds plus testing on each supported platform. It is not needed for ordinary JavaScript/TypeScript application logic.

The Expo Modules API creates Swift and Kotlin module code. Follow current official documentation and generated examples; do not hand-invent project integration or assume one platform implementation covers the other.

preserve: Keep the generated package manifest, lockfile, Expo app configuration, route structure, TypeScript configuration, assets, scripts and SDK-compatible dependency set; record intentional changes.

Preserve the selected Git repository boundary. The current create-expo-app CLI has no documented --no-git option and the reviewed scaffold created an initial Git repository and commit; inspect this before adding it to a monorepo or existing source tree.
Keep platform identifiers, entitlements, permission descriptions, config plugins, native modules and app-version/build-number policy explicit and compatible with both targets.

Do not commit signing keys, local credentials, generated caches or machine-specific SDK paths. Preserve the project lockfile, build configuration and any native project sources the team has chosen to maintain.
verification: Record create-expo-app version, selected template, resolved Expo SDK/React Native/React versions, package manager and installed runtime; inspect the actual generated baseline before editing.
Run the selected Expo compatibility check and Expo Doctor; retain output and resolve version/configuration warnings before native work.

Build/install a development build for iOS and Android. Exercise the same core journeys with both platform navigation, permissions, lifecycle, offline/reconnect and accessibility behavior; a JavaScript bundle or Expo Go pass does not qualify these native targets.
Test the oldest supported iOS/Android versions and current representative devices. Verify app links, push/permission flows and native SDK integrations only when included in the product scope.

Before a release, verify bundle/application identifiers, signing ownership, version/build numbers, privacy declarations, store listing ownership and install/update behavior on both platforms. A local build or cloud build is not store publication.

integration_steps: From the generated project root, record app identifiers, supported platforms/OS versions, runtime, Expo SDK, API contract, permissions and build owner in the project's README. Keep the actual generated lockfile.

Select the backend independently. Keep database writes, user/resource authorization, AI/provider secrets, email and durable work server-side. Define versioned API responses and controlled client error handling; a mobile app binary is inspectable.

Implement route/screen state and API access behind testable modules. Keep device UI and domain rules separated enough to test shared logic, but do not abstract away meaningful iOS/Android interaction differences.

Add a native dependency only for a stated capability. Check both-platform support, config plugin, SDK compatibility and minimum OS/API before adding it. Build a development client instead of expecting Expo Go to contain it.

If offline behavior is required, specify local sources, accepted stale data, queued operations, conflict resolution, account switching and data deletion before choosing storage libraries. Server remains the authority for protected/shared data.

Run shared unit/API tests and build/install both native targets. Test navigation/back, permission denial, app restart, expired/revoked sessions, network loss/recovery and accessibility with representative emulators/simulators and physical devices.

Separate development, preview and production application identifiers as needed. Establish account/credential ownership, app store policy and update compatibility before preparing signed builds. No integration, signing or release is implied by generation.
